question.problem:
$$
f(r,\theta )=⟨\text{_____},\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,r⟩,\,r\ge 0
$$

The vector-valued function $f(r,\theta )$ above parametrizes the half-cone defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${z}^{2}={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ for $z\ge 0.$ What is the first component of $f?$
question.worked_solution:
In cylindrical polar coordinates, the given half-cone has the equation

$$
z=r.
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its $(x,y,z)$ coordinates can be found using the following formulas:

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r,\theta ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩ \\  & =⟨r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,r⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $r\in [0,\infty )$ and $\theta \in [0,2\pi ).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$
